intent: A divider between regions or sections of the sidebar panel.
typical_uses: A line between two groups in SidebarContent, or below the header's switcher

dont_use_when.situation: A divider anywhere outside the sidebar panel

invariants.text: SidebarSeparator is the kit's Separator with the sidebar border color; horizontal, it is inset 8px from each side instead of spanning the full width.

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the separator's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property.

style.states: style accepts a function of the separator's state as well as a plain style object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (orientation). The compiler emits one JSON type per property, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through sidebar.module.css, not through this.

bad.title: A plain Separator in the panel
bad.why: Separator spans the full panel width in the page's border color; SidebarSeparator carries the panel's border color and its 8px inset.

render.description: TS: ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, SeparatorState> | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies. Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the separator's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property.

style.description: TS: CSSProperties | ((state: SeparatorState) => CSSProperties | undefined) | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. style accepts a function of the separator's state as well as a plain style object. Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (orientation). The compiler emits one JSON type per property, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through sidebar.module.css, not through this.
